pr_title: Expose shape property for shape query parameters classes
pr_body:
Exposed properties for both 2D and 3D physics (missing getter).

Related to #15611 (CC @bojidar-bg):

> OS.window_title, **Physics{,2D}ShapeQueryParameters.shape** and Viewport.attach_to_screen_rect lack getters, so I didn't bind them.

Thoughts:
1. ~~Should `shape_rid` be unexposed in favor high-level `shape` member? (4.0)~~ no, see a use case at https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/39846#issuecomment-650121026.
2. The doc gen doesn't seem to respect `Shape[2D]` resource type hints for these properties.

Fixes #39699 (see #39846).
pr_comments:
Perhaps do the same for `Physics2DTestMotionResult::collider_rid` (found by searching for `member.+type="RID` in the docs)?

To make the type match, you should change the type from `RES` to `Shape{,2D}`.

They cannot be removed prior to 4.0, so this part of the change should be tracked in #16863.

Note that the code does not build currently.

> Perhaps do the same for Physics2DTestMotionResult::collider_rid (found by searching for member.+type="RID in the docs)?

Those have the properties already. Or do you mean that they also should be unexposed?

> To make the type match, you should change the type from `RES` to `Shape{,2D}`.

Wouldn't this introduce coupling with scene resources? Also I'm not sure whether it's possible to override default shape implementation. Note that currently it still reports as `Resource` in the docs without this PR. I wonder if it can be made possible for the docs to retrieve custom scene export hint even if the object is represented as a `Ref<Resource>` in that case.

> Note that the code does not build currently.

Works perfectly fine on MSVC... Should be solved with the above suggestion though.

Well, it is possible to force a custom return type by adding `:Type` after the method's name, something like:
```c++
ClassDB::bind_method(D_METHOD("get_shape:Shape2D"), &Physics2DShapeQueryParameters::get_shape);
```

So I was wrong with my assumption that one can convert `RID` to an instance like that, The MSVC compiler was just more permissive and let the `RID` to be converted to a `null` instance in getter...

Updated PR to store the actual reference to the shape resource. I left it as `RES` as it seems like it's possible to implement your own `Shape[2D]` implementation and it shouldn't depend on specific one provided by Godot core I think.

Stumbled upon #39846 which does similar thing except it actually breaks compat in 4.0 as suggested. This PR targeted 3.2 initially so perhaps this can be redone for 3.2 specifically, as it does not break compat.

EDIT: nonetheless, see potential valid use case at https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/39846#issuecomment-650121026.

EDIT2: yeah we've found a valid use case which makes this PR relevant again.
Does this fix #39699 too like #39846 would?

Applied suggestions by @pouleyKetchoupp (added as co-author as well).

Also added some code snippets as in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/39846#issuecomment-650121026.

Tested with 3D as well (interestingly, 2D and 3D have inconsistent API):

```gdscript
extends Node3D

func _ready():
	var rid = PhysicsServer3D.shape_create(PhysicsServer3D.SHAPE_SPHERE)
	var radius = 2.0
	PhysicsServer3D.shape_set_data(rid, radius)
	
	var shape = SphereShape3D.new()
	var params = PhysicsShapeQueryParameters3D.new()
	
	params.shape = shape
	assert(params.shape == shape)
	
	params.shape_rid = rid
	assert(params.shape == null) # Different resources, should be reset.
	
	params.shape = shape
	params.shape_rid = shape.get_rid()
	assert(params.shape == shape) # Not changed, same resource.

```

issue_context.title: Bullet engine PhysicsDirectSpaceState.intersect_shape() crash with no errors
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues for potential duplicates before filing yours:	
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue	
-->

**Godot version:**
Godot 3.2.1 Stable 64 Bit
<!-- Specify commit hash if using non-official build. -->


**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10
<!-- Specify GPU model, drivers, and the backend (GLES2, GLES3, Vulkan) if graphics-related. -->


**Issue description:**
When performing a intersect_shape query using on the space state using the Bullet physics engine, if the PhysicsShapeQueryParameters object's shape is not set, there is a crash with no errors. Using the GodotPhysics physics engine, the error "get: Condition "!p_rid.is_valid()" is true." is outputted to the debugger. Also, this may or may not be a bug, setting the shape of the physics parameters object does not add to the reference counter of the shape, so if the shape was created locally and set to the physics parameter object inside that same scope, when the shape is freed it causes the same crash when using the BulletPhysics engine. PhysicsShapeQueryParameters.set_shape() isn't referencing the shape directly. Maybe that isn't a bug, it just seems that way because of the Bullet engine crash.
<!-- What happened, and what was expected. -->


**Steps to reproduce:**
I created a project with three nodes. NoShapeSet has a script that performs an intersect_shape with no shape set. ShapeReferenceLost sets the shape in the local scope of a setup function so that the shape reference is lost before the intersect_shape is performed. ShapeReferenceHeld holds a reference to the shape in a script variable and set it to the physics parameters object to act as the control. No crash happens when running the test with only this node's test enabled.

I added two export variables to enable/disable the test on each node and to set whether the intersect_shape is run just once or every frame.

A simple workaround would be to just make sure all query parameters have shapes set and that all shapes used aren't accidently freed, but without error outputs, it took me a bit to track down what caused it in my personal project I am working on. So, a proper fix would be better.

**Minimal reproduction project:**
<!-- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue. Drag and drop a zip archive to upload it. -->
[PhysicsBug.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/4807332/PhysicsBug.zip)
comments:
I've just made PR #39747 to fix the crashes with invalid shapes and replace them with errors.

Note: The case where a shape has been released and is still referenced in query parameters will trigger the same error. Fixing it is possible, but it would mean storing a shape reference in the query parameters and probably requires to break compatibility (remove `PhysicsShapeQueryParameters::set_shape_rid` as it makes it more complicated to store a reference).

Does this need a fix or is this intended behavior? The physics server function calls all operate on RIDs passed to the functions to create or modify different physics shapes and bodies. Although, I can see how this is different because you're not directlty interfacing with the server and are using a object which could hold a reference to the shape and then perform the calls to the physics server by passing the shapes RID from the reference it would hold.
I think it makes sense to fix it. I just haven't looked into the details yet because it's a bit more involved.
I've just opened PR #39846 to properly fix this issue for 4.0.
I've closed my new PR as @Xrayez already made a fix for this issue in PR #35633 some time ago and it doesn't break compatibility.

review_comments: `shape_ref` should be reset in `set_shape_rid` to keep things consistent.
Yes that's what I meant! And I agree, it's safer to first check if there's a stored shape and if the rid is different.
Same thing here, `shape_ref` should be reset in `set_shape_rid` to keep things consistent.
